To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

breast cancer survivors perceived three practices as particularly helpful during their return-to work process: maintaining communication, working with them to plan their return-to-work and providing them with flexibility at the beginning.

the three main practices put into place by their supervisors that breast cancer survivors found helpful during the return to work process were: (1) keeping in contact with them during their period of leave; (2) helping them to organize their return to work before their actual return to work; and (3), allowing them flexibility in the beginning of their return to work.

the practices of maintaining communication, working together to structure the return-to-work, and allowing flexibility are perceived as particularly helpful by breast cancer patients in the return-to-work.

the practices put in place by supervisors to support breast cancer survivors in the return-to-work are perceived as helpful by the survivors.

the practices perceived as being helpful by breast cancer patients during their return to work are maintaining communication during their absence, working with them to plan their return-to-work before their actual return and allowing them flexibility in the schedule at the beginning of their return-to-work.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the practices of maintaining communication during their absence, working with them to plan their return to work and allowing them flexibility in schedule were perceived as particularly helpful by the participants.
supervisors play a critical role in supporting breast cancer survivors during the return-to work process and should be involved in developing services to help them in this regard.

breast cancer survivors perceive that the practices of maintaining communication, working with them to prepare their return to work, and allowing them flexibility in scheduling are particularly helpful during their return-to work process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
employers should maintain communication with their employees during their period of illness and should also provide flexibility in their schedule at the beginning of their return to work.
employers should be aware of their role in supporting breast cancer survivors during this process.
supervisors are key players in the return-to-work of breast cancer survivors.
